heading: First Impressions
source: Bài đọc phỏng theo Basic Manners – Ann Ingalls (The Child's World, 2013), tr. 4–9.

paras.label: A
paras.text: Have you ever wondered why some people seem to make friends easily, while others {struggle|struggle}? Often, the answer is surprisingly simple: good manners. Manners are not a set of boring rules invented by adults. They are small actions that show other people you {respect|respect} them. If you pay attention to how people treat each other, and think about how you would like to be treated, you will soon understand what good manners look like. Of course, you will sometimes see people {act like a goon|goon}, but that doesn't mean you have to copy them.

paras.label: B
paras.text: When a {guest|guest} arrives at your home, the first few seconds matter. A friendly "Hello" and a warm smile tell your visitor that you are glad they came. Shaking hands is {a nice touch|touch}, but be careful: a handshake should be {firm|firm}, not so strong that you {rattle their brains|rattle}! However, greetings are not the same everywhere. In China, for example, smiling at someone you don't know well can be seen as {rude|rude}, so what feels friendly in one country may feel strange in another.

paras.label: C
paras.text: A good conversation is like a game of tennis: each person gets a turn. While someone is speaking, stay quiet and really listen instead of planning what you will say next. If you have a question, wait until the speaker has finished. Shouting "My turn!" or "Me, me, me!" might get {attention|attention}, but it won't make people want to listen to you.

paras.label: D
paras.text: The same idea applies when you are standing in a {queue|queue}, whether it is at the school canteen or for a ride at a theme park. There is usually enough room for everyone, so there is no need to push. Someone who behaves like a {bulldozer|bulldozer}, knocking others out of the way to get to the front, may arrive first, but they will probably end up with fewer friends.

paras.label: E
paras.text: The good news is that manners are a skill, and like any skill, they get easier with practice. If you start now, polite behaviour will become a {habit|habit} that stays with you for the rest of your life.

vocab.vi: cư xử ngớ ngẩn, thô lỗ
một điểm cộng nhỏ, chi tiết tinh tế
lắc mạnh (nói đùa: lắc đến “long não”)
xe ủi đất (ở đây: người chen lấn, xô đẩy)

parts.title: Part 1 · Matching headings
parts.instr: Chọn tiêu đề phù hợp nhất cho mỗi đoạn A–E. Có 2 tiêu đề thừa.
options: Why being polite helps you
Making visitors feel welcome
Listening is part of talking
Getting in line without pushing
Practice makes it permanent
How to reach the front first
Strange food in other countries

items.label: Paragraph A
items.why: Đoạn A giải thích vì sao phép lịch sự quan trọng: giúp ta kết bạn và cho người khác thấy ta *respect them*.

items.label: Paragraph B
items.why: Đoạn B nói cách chào khách: *A friendly "Hello" and a warm smile tell your visitor that you are glad they came* = làm khách thấy được chào đón.

items.label: Paragraph C
items.why: Đoạn C khuyên *stay quiet and really listen* khi người khác nói: lắng nghe cũng là một phần của cuộc trò chuyện.

items.label: Paragraph D
items.why: Đoạn D nói về xếp hàng: *there is no need to push*. Tiêu đề "How to reach the front first" là bẫy: bài khuyên điều ngược lại.

items.label: Paragraph E
items.why: Đoạn E: *they get easier with practice* và sẽ thành *a habit… for the rest of your life* = luyện tập thì sẽ thành thói quen lâu dài.

parts.title: Part 2 · Reading comprehension
parts.instr: Chọn đáp án đúng hoặc True / False theo bài đọc.

questions.q: According to paragraph A, how can you learn what good manners look like?
options: by watching others and thinking about how you want to be treated
by memorising a list of rules from adults
by copying everything your classmates do
by reading books about famous people
questions.why: Đoạn A: *If you pay attention to how people treat each other, and think about how you would like to be treated…* Bài còn nói manners **không phải** là luật lệ nhàm chán do người lớn đặt ra.

questions.q: The writer thinks manners are boring rules that adults invented for children.
questions.why: Sai. Đoạn A nói rõ: *Manners are not a set of boring rules invented by adults.*

questions.q: Why does the writer mention China in paragraph B?
options: to show that polite behaviour can be different in different cultures
to say that people in China never smile
to explain why handshakes should be firm
to suggest that smiling is always rude
questions.why: Câu sau giải thích ý đó: *what feels friendly in one country may feel strange in another*. Các lựa chọn khác nói quá (never, always) hoặc không liên quan.

questions.q: In paragraph C, why is a good conversation compared to **a game of tennis**?
options: Each person takes a turn.
One person always wins.
It needs a lot of energy.
People must speak very fast.
questions.why: Ngay sau phép so sánh: *each person gets a turn* – giống như đánh bóng qua lại, mỗi người đến lượt mình.

questions.q: According to paragraph D, a person who pushes may get to the front first but may lose friends.
questions.why: Đúng. *…may arrive first, but they will probably end up with fewer friends.*

questions.q: What is the writer's main purpose in this text?
options: to persuade young readers that good manners help them get on with others
to compare greetings in different countries
to tell a story about a rude child
to explain how to win games at school
questions.why: Cả bài (A–E) đều thuyết phục bạn đọc nhỏ tuổi rằng phép lịch sự giúp kết bạn và được quý mến. Văn hoá Trung Quốc chỉ là một ví dụ nhỏ trong đoạn B.

parts.title: Part 3 · Picture tasks
parts.instr: Quan sát tranh minh hoạ trong sách và trả lời.

questions.alt: A girl shaking a boy's hand very hard while saying Hello
questions.q: Look at the boy's face and the lines around him. Which piece of advice from paragraph B has the girl forgotten?
options: A handshake should not be too strong.
You should always say "Hello".
You should smile at your guest.
Shaking hands is impolite.
questions.why: Các nét rung và gương mặt hoảng hốt của cậu bé cho thấy cô bé bắt tay quá mạnh, như kiểu *rattle their brains*. Cô bé vẫn nói Hello và vẫn cười, nên hai phương án về lời chào và nụ cười không đúng.

questions.alt: A girl pushing two children aside and shouting Me, me, me
questions.q: Which word from the text best describes the girl in the middle?
options: a bulldozer
a guest
a good listener
a tennis player
questions.why: Cô bé đẩy hai bạn sang hai bên và hét *Me, me, me!*, đúng kiểu *behaves like a bulldozer, knocking others out of the way* ở đoạn D.

questions.alt: A girl walking towards two friends on a bench, all waving and smiling
questions.q: The girl is meeting her friends. Why would the writer say this is a good greeting?
options: Her smile and wave show she is glad to see them.
She is running to get there before anyone else.
She is waiting quietly for her turn to speak.
She is shaking hands firmly with everyone.
questions.why: Đoạn B: *a warm smile tell[s] your visitor that you are glad they came.* Trong tranh cô bé cười và vẫy tay, các bạn cũng vui vẻ đáp lại.

parts.title: Part 4 · Gapped text
parts.instr: Đọc đoạn văn mới dưới đây và chọn câu phù hợp cho mỗi chỗ trống. Có 2 câu thừa.
parts.text: Last week, our teacher asked the class a question about the school trip. Minh knew the answer, so he immediately shouted it out. [1] Lan, on the other hand, waited until the teacher had finished speaking. [2] When it was her turn, everyone listened carefully to what she said. [3]
options: Unfortunately, nobody heard him because three other students were shouting too.
Then she raised her hand quietly and waited to be chosen.
It showed that patience often gets you more attention than noise.
She pushed past the others to get to the front of the room.
Everyone thanked him for answering so quickly.

items.why: Câu trước nói Minh hét câu trả lời; câu (a) nói kết quả: không ai nghe thấy vì nhiều bạn cùng hét. Câu "Everyone thanked him…" mâu thuẫn với ý của bài (đoạn C).
Lan *waited until the teacher had finished speaking*, rồi *Then she raised her hand quietly* – từ **Then** nối tiếp hành động. Câu "pushed past the others" trái với cách cư xử của Lan.
Câu cuối rút ra bài học từ hai cách cư xử: kiên nhẫn được chú ý hơn ồn ào – đúng thông điệp của đoạn C trong bài đọc.

parts.title: Part 5 · Words in context
parts.instr: Đoán nghĩa của cụm từ dựa vào ngữ cảnh trong bài.

questions.q: *You will sometimes see people act like a goon* (A). What does **act like a goon** mean?
options: behave in a silly or rude way
behave in a brave way
act in a school play
copy good behaviour
questions.why: Câu sau: *that doesn't mean you have to copy them* – tức đây là cách cư xử xấu, không nên bắt chước. **Goon** = người cư xử ngớ ngẩn, thô lỗ.

questions.q: *Shaking hands is a nice touch* (B). What is **a nice touch**?
options: a small extra thing that makes something better
a very important rule you must follow
a way of touching someone gently
something that makes people feel nervous
questions.why: Bắt tay không bắt buộc (câu trước đã đủ: Hello + nụ cười) nhưng là **điểm cộng nhỏ** làm lời chào tốt hơn.

questions.q: *…not so strong that you rattle their brains!* (B). Why does the writer use this phrase?
options: to make a funny exaggeration about a very hard handshake
to warn that handshakes can cause serious injuries
to explain how the brain works
to show that the guest is angry
questions.why: Đây là cách nói phóng đại hài hước (dấu ! cũng gợi ý giọng đùa): bắt tay mạnh quá như làm "lắc não" người ta, chứ không phải gây chấn thương thật.

credit: Tranh minh hoạ: Ronnie Rooney, trong Basic Manners (The Child's World, 2013). Dùng cho mục đích học tập.
